{
  "verdict": "needs-attention",
  "summary": "Static review only; no tools or tests were run. The shown authorization checks, org-bound AES-GCM, and basic Microsoft request construction look sound. Findings concern credential-bearing error propagation, Preview overwriting production ciphertext, and concurrent settings/test updates.",
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Do not propagate unrestricted Graph error text",
      "severity": "high",
      "confidence": 0.97,
      "file": "src/lib/email/graph-mail.ts",
      "line_start": 66,
      "line_end": 72,
      "failure_scenario": "Graph returns an error containing the access token, for example error.message = \"Rejected token token-123\" -> sendFailure preserves it -> sendOrgEmail logs it, and sendTestEmail stores it in last_test_error and returns it to the browser.",
      "body": "The confidentiality guarantee depends on upstream diagnostic text never containing credentials. Truncating to 300 characters does not enforce that guarantee. The test named \"no failure detail ever carries the secret or the access token\" supplies only \"Access is denied.\" on the Graph path; its actual credential-echo input exercises only Entra error_description. It therefore misses this disclosure path. This finding establishes the data flow, not that ordinary Microsoft responses currently echo tokens.",
      "recommendation": "Use explicitly allowlisted error identifiers and locally generated messages for logs, persisted errors, and action responses. Discard arbitrary upstream messages. Add fixtures containing the secret and token in Graph error fields and assert their absence from every output sink."
    },
    {
      "title": "Prevent Preview from replacing production ciphertext under another key",
      "severity": "high",
      "confidence": 1.0,
      "file": "src/app/dashboard/settings/actions.ts",
      "line_start": 42,
      "line_end": 45,
      "failure_scenario": "Production settings use key K1, while a Preview sharing production data uses K2 -> the Preview test reports secret_unreadable and instructs the admin to paste the secret again -> saving replaces the shared ciphertext with a K2 ciphertext -> Production can no longer send organizational email.",
      "body": "The inline deployment notes explicitly allow this unresolved configuration. Saving checks only whether a row exists; it does not establish that this deployment's key is compatible with the existing settings. Both keys produce the same v1 envelope, and the recovery instruction actively leads an admin toward overwriting working production credentials.",
      "recommendation": "Resolve and enforce the environment policy before deployment: isolate Preview data, or prohibit Preview mutations against production. If writable data is deliberately shared, require the same encryption key and validate that requirement. Diagnose key mismatch before recommending secret replacement."
    },
    {
      "title": "Reject stale saves before retaining the current secret",
      "severity": "medium",
      "confidence": 1.0,
      "file": "src/app/dashboard/settings/actions.ts",
      "line_start": 55,
      "line_end": 66,
      "failure_scenario": "Two admins open the same settings. Admin A saves a new client ID and its new secret. Admin B subsequently saves an old form with a blank secret -> B restores the old client ID while retaining A's new ciphertext -> the credential pair no longer matches, and subsequent email sends fail.",
      "body": "Blank-on-save preserves the secret currently in the database, while every other field comes from the submitting browser's potentially stale snapshot. The existence read and unconditional update cannot detect this combination. This can also overwrite the newly entered expiry date and produce incorrect renewal warnings.",
      "recommendation": "Include a configuration revision in the settings view and require an atomic revision match when saving. Return a conflict without changing data when the form is stale. Also require an explicit secret replacement when changing its tenant/client identity."
    },
    {
      "title": "Record test results only against the configuration tested",
      "severity": "medium",
      "confidence": 1.0,
      "file": "src/app/dashboard/settings/actions.ts",
      "line_start": 89,
      "line_end": 96,
      "failure_scenario": "A test reads working configuration A and waits for Microsoft. Another save installs configuration B with an invalid secret and clears the previous test result. The A request then succeeds -> this unconditional update marks B's current settings as successfully tested -> the admin sees success although subsequent sends using B fail.",
      "body": "The result update identifies only the organization. It has no connection to the credential/configuration snapshot used by sendOrgEmail, so an in-flight test can undo the save action's deliberate invalidation of test evidence. Disabling buttons in one browser would not protect against another tab or admin.",
      "recommendation": "Carry the tested configuration revision through the send operation and condition the result write on that revision still being current. If settings changed, report that the result belongs to the previous configuration and require a new test."
    }
  ],
  "next_steps": [
    "Replace unrestricted diagnostic propagation and add credential-echo regression cases.",
    "Enforce the Preview/Production database and encryption-key policy before deployment.",
    "Add configuration revisions and exercise overlapping saves and test-result writes.",
    "After fixes, complete the planned production access probe and real Microsoft delivery test."
  ]
}
